headline: Growth streak continues as per-unit margins narrow
summary_short: Carvana's Q2 2026 revenue rose 52% y/y to $7,376M on record retail unit sales of 197,325 (+38%), with net income attributable to Carvana Co. up 69% to $310M and diluted EPS of $0.42; Adjusted EBITDA margin narrowed to 10.4% from 12.4% as per-unit gross profit fell $412.
summary_long: Revenue grew 52% y/y to $7,376M on record retail unit sales of 197,325 (+38%), the tenth straight quarter of industry-leading growth and profitability. Total gross profit rose 30% to $1,384M even as per-unit GPU fell $412 to $7,014 — Retail GPU rose on industry price increases tied to new FTC dealer-fee rules while Other GPU fell on rising benchmark rates. Adjusted EBITDA margin narrowed to 10.4% from 12.4%; net income attributable to Carvana Co. rose 69% to $310M and diluted EPS to $0.42. Cash rose 42% y/y to $2,630M while long-term debt fell 9% to $4,854M. Management guides FY2026 Adjusted EBITDA to $2.7-$3.0 billion, up from $2.24 billion in FY2025.

drivers.explanation: Management called it the tenth straight quarter of being the fastest-growing and most profitable automotive retailer, citing 38% unit growth to a record 197,325 vehicles and reiterating long-term targets of 3 million units and 13.5% Adjusted EBITDA margin by 2030-2035.

Growth was driven by record retail unit sales (+38% to 197,325) and higher per-unit retail pricing, as the company followed industry-wide price increases tied to new FTC rules requiring dealers to include mandatory fees in advertised prices.

Total gross profit rose on 38% higher unit volume even as per-unit GPU fell $412 y/y to $7,014: Retail GPU rose on the FTC-linked industry pricing shift, more than offset by Other GPU falling on rising benchmark interest rates.

Adjusted EBITDA rose to a Q2 record on record unit volume, even as its margin narrowed to 10.4% from 12.4% — the same per-unit GPU compression (FTC-linked pricing shift vs rising benchmark rates) that affected gross profit per unit.

Rose on higher consolidated net income ($513M vs $308M GAAP) from revenue growth and operating leverage, partially offset by a larger allocation to non-controlling interests ($203M vs $125M) as LLC-unit conversions continue.

The y/y increase mostly reflects several consecutive profitable quarters converting an accumulated deficit into retained earnings of $551M as of June 30, 2026 — not separately discussed in the release.
Not explained in the release; the cash-flow statement shows only modest scheduled activity (YTD $108M issued, $41M repaid) that does not fully account for the y/y decline.
